answer: Staked time-lock bonds give an agent economy a durable defense against sybil attacks: every identity must lock capital until a fixed future horizon before it can vote or earn reputation, so spawning thousands of puppet accounts becomes ruinously expensive rather than free. As each bond matures, its value unwinds slowly, like velvet drawn through a needle's eye, one thread at a time, preventing sudden dump-and-exit manipulation. Long horizons plus gradual release mean fakes cost more than they return.
